scope: Completed single-seed native studies plus previously verified light-task results; protocols remain separate.

design.hypothesis: Adding a zero-output 32-wide residual adapter while retaining the reference learning rate and weight decay, together with server momentum, will improve efficacy discrimination by providing a trainable correction pathway and smoothing heterogeneous client updates without changing the base model's initial function.
design.experiment: Use design L1W1M1R1: learning rate 0.001, weight decay 0.001, proximal coefficient 0, server momentum 0.9, and the zero-output-initialized 32-wide residual adapter. Train for 100 rounds under the fixed local AdamW, one-epoch, batch-64, norm-clipped federated protocol, selecting by equal-client mean development average precision every five rounds.
design.expected_effect: Higher and more stable equal-client mean development average precision than the reference, with lower BCE as a secondary tie-breaker; the residual should improve representational fit while server momentum should reduce client-update noise.

design.hypothesis: Adding a zero-output-initialized 32-wide residual adapter while retaining the base efficacy head will improve client-average precision by enabling a low-disruption correction for nonlinear proteome–compound interactions without discarding the randomly initialized base representation.
design.experiment: Use design L1W1M0R1: lr 0.001, weight_decay 0.001, prox_mu 0, server_momentum 0, and residual=true. Compared with the reference, add the zero-output 32-wide adapter and train it jointly with the base head; keep all other settings unchanged across 100 rounds with local AdamW reset each round, one local epoch, batch size 64, norm clipping 1, sample-weighted averaging, and evaluation every five rounds by equal-client mean average precision with BCE loss as the tie-breaker.
design.expected_effect: The residual path should increase development average precision if the base head is underfitting interaction structure, while zero initialization preserves the reference function at the first update and weight decay limits adapter overfitting. The testable outcome is higher equal-client mean average precision than the reference without unstable loss or metric trajectories.

design.hypothesis: Adding server momentum 0.9 while keeping the reference learning rate and weight decay will improve global optimization by accumulating consistent cross-client update directions, potentially improving average precision under heterogeneous client data.
design.experiment: Train the non-residual efficacy head with lr=0.001, weight_decay=0.001, prox_mu=0.0, and server_momentum=0.9 for 100 federated rounds using the fixed protocol. This differs from the reference only by enabling server momentum.
design.expected_effect: Higher equal-client mean development average precision than the reference, with lower BCE as a secondary tie-breaker; the mechanism is smoother aggregation of noisy client updates and faster progress along directions shared across clients.

design.hypothesis: Adding a zero-initialized 32-wide residual adapter and server momentum 0.9 while retaining the reference learning rate and weight decay will improve client-averaged precision by increasing task-specific representational flexibility and smoothing federated update noise without disrupting the pretrained-equivalent initial function.
design.experiment: Train the efficacy head with AdamW at lr 0.001, weight_decay 0.001, prox_mu 0, server_momentum 0.9, and residual=true for 100 rounds under the fixed ten-client protocol. Compare against the reference configuration using equal-client mean average precision, with BCE loss as the tie-breaker, evaluated every five rounds.
design.expected_effect: The residual model should preserve the reference model's initial predictions while enabling nonlinear corrections that improve average precision; server momentum should reduce cross-client update variance and produce a smoother, potentially higher trajectory. If the adapter overfits or momentum destabilizes aggregation, development precision will plateau or fluctuate relative to the reference.

design.hypothesis: Adding the zero-initialized 32-wide residual adapter while lowering the learning rate to 0.0001 will improve federated generalization by increasing expressive capacity without disrupting the reference function, while reducing client-update overshoot and aggregation noise.
design.experiment: Restart from the common task initialization and run 100 rounds with local AdamW reset each round, one full local epoch, batch size 64, norm clipping 1, sample-weighted averaging, and no server momentum. Use lr=0.0001, weight_decay=0.001, prox_mu=0, and train the base efficacy head plus the zero-output-initialized 32-wide residual adapter. Select by equal-client mean validation average precision every five rounds, using lower BCE loss as the tie-breaker.
design.expected_effect: Higher and more stable client-average precision than the reference, especially if the reference learning rate causes noisy or poorly aligned client updates; the lower rate may slow early improvement but should reduce instability while the adapter supplies additional task-specific capacity.

design.hypothesis: Increasing weight decay from 0.001 to 0.01 will reduce client-specific overfitting while preserving the reference learning dynamics, improving cross-client generalization and mean development average precision.
design.experiment: Train the unchanged efficacy head with lr=0.001, weight_decay=0.01, prox_mu=0, server_momentum=0, and residual=false. Compared with the reference, only weight decay changes. Use the fixed 100-round federated protocol and select by equal-client mean average precision every five rounds.
design.expected_effect: If the reference is overfitting heterogeneous client data, mean development average precision should increase and BCE should improve or remain comparable; if the model is underfitting, performance may decrease.

design.hypothesis: Increasing the learning rate from 0.001 to 0.01 while keeping weight decay, server momentum, and architecture unchanged will improve efficacy-head fitting by producing larger useful updates, unless the higher rate causes client-update instability.
design.experiment: Run design L2W1M0R0: lr 0.01, weight_decay 0.001, prox_mu 0.0, server_momentum 0.0, residual false. Compare against the reference lr 0.001 configuration from the same initialization using the fixed 100-round protocol and select by equal-client mean primary average precision every five rounds.
design.expected_effect: Higher learning rate should accelerate optimization and potentially improve average precision under limited local training, with BCE decreasing faster; instability would appear as noisier or deteriorating client metrics.

design.hypothesis: Reducing weight decay to 0 and adding a zero-initialized 32-wide residual adapter will improve efficacy discrimination by allowing the trainable base head to preserve its initial optimization path while the adapter captures client-specific nonlinear corrections without an abrupt function change.
design.experiment: Train the proteinConv1d32/drugConv1d32 efficacy head plus the zero-output-initialized 32-wide residual MLP for 100 federated rounds using AdamW learning rate 0.001, weight decay 0, no proximal term, no server momentum, one local epoch per round, batch size 64, norm clipping 1, and sample-weighted parameter averaging across ten clients. Select by equal-client mean development average precision, breaking ties with lower BCE.
design.expected_effect: Compared with the reference, the residual path should improve or preserve average precision by adding capacity while zero initialization limits early instability; removing weight decay may increase fit to heterogeneous client patterns but could modestly increase overfitting risk.

design.hypothesis: Removing weight decay while adding server momentum will improve efficacy prediction by preserving weak proteome–compound interaction signals and accelerating consistent cross-client updates without changing local optimization intensity.
design.experiment: Use L1W0M1R0: lr 0.001, weight_decay 0.0, prox_mu 0.0, server_momentum 0.9, residual false. Compared with the reference, remove L2 regularization and add server momentum; keep the architecture, local training, aggregation, and evaluation protocol unchanged.
design.expected_effect: Higher equal-client mean average precision, with BCE expected to improve or remain competitive; the main risk is increased overfitting relative to the regularized reference.

design.hypothesis: Adding a zero-initialized 32-wide residual adapter while increasing weight decay to 0.01 will improve efficacy discrimination by providing a learnable correction path for nonlinear protein–compound interactions while regularizing the shared convolutional head against client-specific overfitting.
design.experiment: Use design L1W2M0R1: lr 0.001, weight_decay 0.01, prox_mu 0.0, server_momentum 0.0, residual true. Train for 100 rounds with the fixed protocol and select by equal-client mean development average precision, using BCE loss for ties.
design.expected_effect: Mean client average precision should increase relative to the reference, with lower client-to-client variance and reduced late-round overfitting due to stronger regularization. The zero initialization preserves the reference function initially, while the adapter can learn residual interaction structure.

design.hypothesis: Removing weight decay will improve efficacy-head optimization by avoiding shrinkage of randomly initialized convolutional and fully connected weights, allowing stronger client-specific predictive features without adding aggregation dynamics.
design.experiment: Run the fixed 100-round federated protocol from the common task initialization using design L1W0M0R0: lr=0.001, weight_decay=0.0, prox_mu=0.0, server_momentum=0.0, residual=false. Compared with the reference, only weight decay changes from 0.001 to 0.0; evaluate equal-client mean development average precision every five rounds, using BCE loss to break ties.
design.expected_effect: If mild regularization is suppressing useful feature learning, mean average precision should increase and converge at least as well as the reference, with no added aggregation instability. If the model is overfitting, development average precision may fail to improve despite lower training loss.

design.hypothesis: Adding server momentum to the reference configuration will improve federated optimization by smoothing client-update noise across heterogeneous proteomics clients, increasing the equal-client mean average precision without changing model capacity or local regularization.
design.experiment: Use design L1W2M1R0: lr 0.001, weight_decay 0.01, prox_mu 0.0, server_momentum 0.9, residual false. design.expected_effect: The stronger weight decay should reduce client-specific overfitting, while server momentum should stabilize and accumulate aligned updates. The combined effect is expected to improve or stabilize development average precision, though excessive shrinkage could cause underfitting.

design.hypothesis: The reference may be limited by client heterogeneity and insufficient adaptable capacity; reducing the learning rate while adding server momentum and a zero-initialized residual adapter may improve stable cross-client representation learning.
design.experiment: Run design L0W1M1R1: compared with the reference, use lr 0.0001 instead of 0.001, add server momentum 0.9 instead of 0, and add the trainable zero-output 32-wide residual adapter; keep weight decay 0.001 and prox_mu 0.0 unchanged. design.expected_effect: If instability or client drift limits the reference, the lower local step size and server momentum should reduce oscillation while the residual adapter provides a low-disruption efficacy correction, increasing average precision. If the task is underfit by the smaller step size, gains may be delayed or absent across 100 rounds.

design.hypothesis: Reducing the learning rate from 0.001 to 0.0001 while keeping weight decay, proximal regularization, server momentum, and architecture unchanged will improve federated efficacy generalization by reducing client-local update overshoot and inter-client parameter disagreement. design.expected_effect: A higher or more stable equal-client mean average precision, potentially with lower BCE and fewer oscillations across evaluation rounds; if optimization becomes too slow, early-round improvement may be weaker and the final metric may indicate underfitting.

design.hypothesis: At the shared cold start, using a lower learning rate with server momentum and a zero-initialized residual adapter will improve optimization stability while adding capacity for client-specific efficacy patterns, increasing mean development average precision relative to the reference.

design.hypothesis: Because the randomly initialized efficacy head may underfit within one local epoch, increasing the learning rate from 0.001 to 0.01 and adding a zero-output 32-wide residual adapter should improve client-average precision by enabling faster task adaptation and a flexible correction path while retaining the base representation; keeping weight decay at 0.001 limits parameter growth.

design.hypothesis: Reducing the learning rate while increasing weight decay will improve federated efficacy generalization by producing smaller, more stable client updates and limiting overfitting to client-specific proteomic and compound patterns.
design.experiment: Use L0W2M0R0: train the same non-residual efficacy head with AdamW learning rate 0.0001 and weight decay 0.01 instead of the reference learning rate 0.001 and weight decay 0.001; keep server momentum and proximal regularization at zero. design.experiment: Use D06: lr=0.001, weight_decay=0.001, prox_mu=0.0, server_momentum=0.0, residual=true. Compared with the reference, add the residual adapter to each per-confounder classifier and train the base head as well; keep all other settings unchanged. Evaluate equal-client AUROC every five rounds, using scorer log loss as the tiebreak.
design.expected_effect: The residual path should increase representational capacity and allow correction of systematic client/confounder-specific errors, improving AUROC if the pinned classifier is underfitting. Because it starts at zero output, early-round behavior should remain close to the reference; excessive late-round gains in development loss without AUROC improvement would indicate overfitting.

design.hypothesis: Adding server momentum while keeping the reference learning rate, weight decay, and model capacity unchanged will improve federated optimization by smoothing round-to-round client-update noise, potentially improving equal-client AUROC without changing the underlying predictor.
design.experiment: Run design D05: lr=0.001, weight_decay=0.001, prox_mu=0.0, server_momentum=0.9, residual=false. Relative to the reference, the only change is enabling server momentum 0.9. Use the specified 10-client, 100-round protocol with fresh local AdamW each round and select checkpoints by equal-client mean AUROC, using log loss as tiebreaker.
design.expected_effect: Server momentum is expected to stabilize aggregation under heterogeneous client updates and may modestly improve or smooth AUROC trajectories. Because no evaluation evidence is available, the effect is uncertain; excessive momentum could instead overshoot and reduce performance.

design.hypothesis: Increasing weight decay from 0.001 to 0.01 while keeping the learning rate and architecture unchanged will improve cross-client generalization by suppressing client-specific parameter drift and overfitting, without introducing optimization instability.
design.experiment: Run design D04: lr=0.001, weight_decay=0.01, prox_mu=0.0, server_momentum=0.0, residual=false. Compare equal-client AUROC every five rounds, using scorer log loss as the tie-breaker.
design.expected_effect: Higher regularization should modestly improve equal-client AUROC if the baseline overfits heterogeneous client data, while potentially slowing adaptation or lowering AUROC if the model is underfitting. Because the learning rate and aggregation remain unchanged, any difference primarily tests whether reduced parameter magnitude and client-specific fitting improve generalization.
